provider: Clear Street Trading API / read-only MCP
evidence: Clear Street's official 2026 changelog states GET /v1/market-data/snapshot reports the venue currently holding the national best bid and best offer (NBBO), with separate bid_venue/ask_venue and bid_timestamp/ask_timestamp exchange times.
The same snapshot exposes the last-sale trade venue and exchange timestamp. This is an unusually strong strict-B schema: bid, ask and last have independent exchange event-time evidence.

Clear Street's official read-only MCP endpoint exposes get_market_data_snapshot and cannot place/cancel orders, making the technical scheduler/read-only surface strong once an eligible account is authenticated.

The MCP/API requires a Clear Street trading account/account entitlement. Public documentation found here does not prove that an unfunded eligible retail account permanently retains the exact realtime NBBO market-data entitlement at $0, nor does it publish a separate exchange/SIP fee waiver/classification for this automated API use.

Clear Street Retail's current Founding Member program requires a $5,000 cash deposit to obtain Founding Member status. This condition cannot be generalized to every future/ordinary retail account, but that particular route fails XRAY's no-funding-condition rule.

Current public sources reviewed do not explicitly establish Turkey-resident retail account eligibility. Non-US tax-resident fields/withholding support in the API prove international tax handling exists but do not prove Turkey onboarding.
Therefore A/B are technically/semantically strong, while C and user-jurisdiction D remain fail-closed until exact unfunded entitlement and Turkey eligibility are primary-source proven.

Clear Street's official Sep. 30, 2026 MCP article says its MCP server is 'included at no cost with every account' and immediately states that the Clear Street MCP offers real-time price data for stocks and options. This materially strengthens strict C for the exact MCP product rather than a generic display platform.

The same official article contrasts typical delayed free MCPs with paid real-time MCPs, then names Clear Street as the broker example that supplies paid-quality MCP capability free with an account; this is product-specific current evidence, not an inference from missing price rows.

Clear Street's retail app release notes add a dedicated Market Data Onboarding Step where users review/select real-time market-data agreements. This proves the retail surface has an explicit exchange/market-data entitlement workflow, but public text reviewed so far does not expose the exact subscriber classification or whether any optional data packages are separately charged.

Clear Street's Form CRS (Jan. 1, 2025) broadly says retail clients may pay 'market data/platform fees'. That older/general disclosure does not identify the 2026 free MCP's exact real-time snapshot entitlement and therefore creates a product-scope ambiguity rather than overriding the newer product-specific 'included at no cost with every account' statement.

Form CRS says the $25,000 minimum applies 'to day trade'; it does not state a general $25,000 account-opening or market-data minimum. The Founding Member $5,000 deposit is likewise a program-membership condition, not proven to be the ordinary retail account minimum.

Clear Street's April 2026 Customer Identification Program accepts non-U.S. passport/country-of-issuance and identification showing nationality/residence, and current API account schemas include country_of_tax_residency. This establishes international-account infrastructure but still does not specifically prove Turkey-resident onboarding.

The Clear Street retail app is distributed in multiple non-U.S. App Store regions and contains dynamic region-restriction checks; distribution is only supporting evidence and cannot substitute for a provider statement that Turkey residents are eligible.

Massive/Polygon's official U.S.-stocks product page lists Clear Street among customer logos. This is only a vendor lead and MUST NOT be treated as proof that Clear Street's current NBBO snapshot is sourced from Massive/Polygon absent a direct product binding.
